methods: equation of chord with given midpoint
statement: Chords of the circle $x^{2}+y^{2}=a^{2}$ are drawn through the fixed point $(p,0)$. Show that the midpoints of all such chords lie on the circle $x^{2}+y^{2}-px=0$.
solution:
Let $(h,k)$ be the midpoint of a chord. The chord of $x^{2}+y^{2}=a^{2}$ with midpoint $(h,k)$ has equation $hx+ky=h^{2}+k^{2}$ (the chord is perpendicular to the radius to its midpoint and passes through $(h,k)$). Because the chord passes through $(p,0)$, we have $hp=h^{2}+k^{2}$, i.e. $h^{2}+k^{2}-ph=0$. Therefore every midpoint $(x,y)$ satisfies $x^{2}+y^{2}-px=0$, which is a circle.
